transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
The Federal Trade Commission has opened an investigation into open AI, anthropic and
other artificial intelligence companies over dangers their technology may pose to consumers.
The AI giants and other tech companies in recent months have disclosed examples of their
AI agents going beyond human instructions, finding their way onto the Internet and hacking
external websites.
The Justice Department says it has filed a complaint of judicial misconduct against multiple
federal judges in Minnesota, the Trump administration's latest salvo against the judiciary.
The department is accusing the judges of violating their ethical duties by speaking out publicly
in an interview with the New York Times and PR's Ryan Lucas reports.
In the New York Times interview, judges on the federal bench in Minnesota talked about
the impact on the court and the rule of law of the Trump administration's immigration
crackdown in Minneapolis early this year.
Now, the Justice Department is accusing the judges of making political statements and
violating their judicial duties.
It also alleges the judges are biased against the Department of Homeland Security.
DOJ wants the Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals, which oversees the federal bench in Minnesota,
to order the judges to be recused from any matters involving DHS.
One of the judges named in the complaint, Patrick Shilts, in a statement rejects the
allegations and says his public comments were well within the judiciary's ethical rules.
Ryan Lucas, NPR News, Washington.
Dr. Nicole Safire, President Trump's third nominee for surgeon general, is moving closer
to confirmation.
A Senate committee advanced the radiologist and former Fox News contributors' nomination
with a 12 to 11 vote.
She stated she believes vaccines are safe, and she doesn't believe they cause autism,
putting her at odds with her possible future boss, Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.
As ballots have started going out in this year's midterm elections, voters say they
have a lot of concerns, including the reliability of the mail and potential federal interference.
But as NPR's Miles Parks reports, turnout in this year's election is still an open question.
Carly Koppas, a Republican who runs voting in Weld County, Colorado, says voters have
a lot of questions right now.
How is this going to work?
How are you going to make sure my ballot's going to be counted?
How am I going to get my ballot?
I'm hearing all of these things.
It's tempting to think an environment like this might dampen turnout, and midterms already
typically see lower turnout compared to presidential election years.
But political scientists say it's not so simple.
In some cases, threats to voting rights can actually spur higher turnout, as people are
extra motivated to vote, and political groups mobilize to respond to the threats.
The highest turnout midterm in modern history was in 2018, during President Trump's first
term.
Miles Parks, NPR News, Washington.
Tropical weather that surged onshore from the Pacific is soaking the U.S., while forecasters
announced yet another hurricane off the coast of Mexico.
Heavy rain continues from Colorado across the Great Plains, with storm totals topping
two inches in places.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
The Senate failed to advance a bill today that sought to address voter worries about
data centers and their impact on energy bills.
The bill fell victim to an election year clash on how best to address the growing concern.
The measure needed 60 votes to advance, but fell short 57 to 43.
Democrats said the bill didn't go far enough to help consumers.
The measure had passed overwhelmingly, 417 to 3 in the House.
A year ago today, a tax credit that helped lower the cost of electric vehicles went away.
NPR's Willa Rubin reports on the impact on car sales.
People heard the EV credit was ending last July.
EV sales spiked, and after it went away, EV sales dropped, but this year they have stabilized.
About 6% of new cars sold every month now are electric.
Meanwhile, sales of hybrid cars this year have gone up by almost 27%, according to automotive
platform Edmunds.
Sal Iqbal is the general sales manager at the Toyota franchise in Massapequa, New York.
He has seen this with a popular minivan that Toyota now only makes as a hybrid.
We used to have to literally beg people to take a Sienna, and now we can't keep them
on the shelf.
Residents with gas engines and battery-powered electric motors are fuel efficient, and they
often have a lower sticker price than many EVs.
Willa Rubin, NPR News.
A dozen impressionist and post-impressionist artworks valued at almost half a billion dollars
are going up for auction.
Sotheby says that works by Vincent Mango and Paul Zayzan are expected to smash records.
In the November 18 sale in New York, the paintings come from a late Argentine art collector.
This is NPR News from Washington.

topics.text: FTC opens investigation into OpenAI, Anthropic and other AI companies over consumer safety dangers
Justice Department files judicial misconduct complaint against multiple federal judges in Minnesota
Dr. Nicole Safire, Trump's third surgeon general nominee, advances in Senate committee vote
Voters express concerns about mail ballot reliability and federal interference in midterm elections
Senate fails to advance bill addressing voter concerns about data centers and energy bills
Electric vehicle sales drop after tax credit ends, but stabilize; hybrid sales surge 27%
Dozen impressionist and post-impressionist artworks valued at half billion dollars going to auction
